searchText: I was working on a test requested by <@360491619402776577> regarding EIP-3860, and the tx pool, the test was supposed to send tx with `initcode>MAX_INITCODE_SIZE` before and after Shanghai, and the `eth_sendRawTransaction` was supposed to accept the tx before the fork and reject it only afterwards, but both geth and nethermind seem to be rejecting it before, and I guess this is ok since this is left to client specific behavior, but just to confirm, are all clients going to do this ? And to clarify, the test is not meant to test transaction inclusion in blocks, only rejection from RPCs, tx pool. I think its okay to reject the tx before the fork. We just merged the change recently so old versions should still be able to execute those transactions I'll also check that newPayloadV2 returns invalid if these txs are included You can actually make a test with the block that has this transaction in the rlp and see if it gets verified on block import Yes, the test already exists in the execution-spec-tests, but I wanted to test the tx pool with this other one, because Marius found a bug where a tx with an initcode exceeding the limit was not rejected

excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content:
I was working on a test requested by <@360491619402776577> regarding EIP-3860, and the tx pool, the test was supposed to send tx with `initcode>MAX_INITCODE_SIZE` before and after Shanghai, and the `eth_sendRawTransaction` was supposed to accept the tx before the fork and reject it only afterwards, but both geth and nethermind seem to be rejecting it before, and I guess this is ok since this is left to client specific behavior, but just to confirm, are all clients going to do this ?

And to clarify, the test is not meant to test transaction inclusion in blocks, only rejection from RPCs, tx pool.

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: I think its okay to reject the tx before the fork. We just merged the change recently so old versions should still be able to execute those transactions

excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content: I'll also check that newPayloadV2 returns invalid if these txs are included

excerpts.author: dimitry8570
excerpts.content: You can actually make a test with the block that has this transaction in the rlp and see if it gets verified on block import

excerpts.author: marioevz
excerpts.content: Yes, the test already exists in the execution-spec-tests, but I wanted to test the tx pool with this other one, because Marius found a bug where a tx with an initcode exceeding the limit was not rejected
